searchDocs.title: Disconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> Connection:Disconnect() → () Disconnects the connection from its signal. local connection = signal:Connect(function() print("fired") end) connection:Disconnect() signal:Fire() -- do nothing

searchDocs.title: Reconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> Connection:Reconnect() → () Reconnects a previously disconnected connection. connection:Disconnect() connection:Reconnect()

searchDocs.title: Getting Started with AcidSignal
searchDocs.content: Getting Started with AcidSignal AcidSignal is a simple and lightweight signal implementation for Roblox. It provides a familiar event-driven API with a thread pool, bound arguments, and connection management via a doubly linked list. Here are some quick links to get started using AcidSignal: Installation guideAPI DocsBasic UsageTips & TricksExamples

searchDocs.title: Basic Signal​
searchDocs.content: local Signal = require(path.to.AcidSignal) local signal = Signal.new() signal:Connect(function(value) print("received:", value) end) signal:Fire("hello") -- received: hello

searchDocs.title: Multiple Connections​
searchDocs.content: local signal = Signal.new() signal:Connect(function(value) print("A:", value) end) signal:Connect(function(value) print("B:", value) end) signal:Fire("hello") -- A: hello -- B: hello

searchDocs.title: Waiting for a Signal​
searchDocs.content: local signal = Signal.new() task.delay(2, function() signal:Fire("done") end) local value = signal:Wait(5) if value then print("signal fired with:", value) else print("timed out!") end

searchDocs.title: Using Once for One-Time Events​
searchDocs.content: local signal = Signal.new() signal:Once(function(player) print("first player joined:", player.Name) end)

searchDocs.title: Bound Args for Context​
searchDocs.content: local signal = Signal.new() local function onDamage(amount, source) print(`took {amount} damage from {source}`) end signal:Connect(onDamage, "fire") signal:Connect(onDamage, "poison") signal:Fire(10) -- took 10 damage from fire -- took 10 damage from poison

searchDocs.title: Cleaning Up​
searchDocs.content: local signal = Signal.new() signal:Connect(function() print("A") end) signal:Connect(function() print("B") end) -- disconnect all at once signal:DisconnectAll()

searchDocs.title: Use Once to Avoid Manual Disconnects​
searchDocs.content: If you only need to react to the first fire, use Once instead of manually disconnecting inside the callback:  -- instead of this local conn conn = signal:Connect(function(value) conn:Disconnect() print("fired:", value) end) -- do this signal:Once(function(value) print("fired:", value) end)

searchDocs.title: Use Wait with a Timeout​
searchDocs.content: Calling Wait without a timeout will yield the current thread forever if the signal never fires. Always pass a timeout when the signal MIGHT not fire:  local value = signal:Wait(5) if not value then warn("signal never fired!") return end

searchDocs.title: Reuse Connections with Reconnect​
searchDocs.content: Instead of creating a new connection every time, you can disconnect and reconnect the same one:  local connection = signal:Connect(function() print("fired") end) connection:Disconnect() -- later... connection:Reconnect()

searchDocs.title: Avoid Firing Inside Callbacks​
searchDocs.content: Calling Fire inside a callback causes reentrancy. AcidSignal allows up to 256 recursive fires before dropping the call with a warning. If you need to fire in response to a fire, consider deferring it:  signal:Connect(function() task.defer(signal.Fire, signal) -- safe, deferred to next frame end)

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Signal.new() → Signal<A...> Creates a new signal. local signal = Signal.new()

searchDocs.title: Connect​
searchDocs.content: </> Signal:Connect( fn: ( A..., V... ) → (),-- The function to call when the signal fires ...: V...-- Extra arguments appended to every call ) → Connection<A...,V...> Connects a callback to the signal. local connection = signal:Connect(function(value) print("fired:", value) end) -- With bound args local connection = signal:Connect(function(value, value2) print(value, value2) end, "hello") signal:Fire("world") -- hello world

searchDocs.title: Once​
searchDocs.content: </> Signal:Once( fn: ( A..., V... ) → (),-- The function to call when the signal fires ...: V...-- Extra arguments appended to every call ) → Connection<A...,V...> Connects a callback that automatically disconnects after the first fire. signal:Once(function(value) print("fired once:", value) end)

searchDocs.title: Wait​
searchDocs.content: </> Signal:Wait( timeout: number?-- Maximum seconds to wait. If reached, returns false. ) → ( boolean,-- Whether the signal fired before the timeout A...-- The arguments passed to Fire, or nil if timed out ) Yields the current thread until the signal fires. -- without timeout task.defer(function() signal:Fire("Example") end) local value = signal:Wait() print(value) -- "Example" -- with timeout (returns nil if timed out) local value = signal:Wait(1) print(value) -- nil

searchDocs.title: Fire​
searchDocs.content: </> Signal:Fire( ...: A...-- Arguments to pass to all connected callbacks ) → () Fires the signal, calling all connected callbacks via the thread pool. If reentrancy exceeds 256 recursive calls, a warning is emitted and the call is dropped. signal:Fire("hello")

searchDocs.title: DisconnectAll​
searchDocs.content: </> Signal:DisconnectAll() → () Disconnects all connections from the signal. signal:DisconnectAll()

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Signal:Destroy() → () Alias for DisconnectAll. signal:Destroy()

searchDocs.title: Method 1. Manual Installation​
searchDocs.content: Download the latest release and place it in your project (e.g., ReplicatedStorage).

searchDocs.title: 1. Add dependency​
searchDocs.content: Add the package to your wally.toml:  [dependencies] AcidSignal = "thecogumeta/acidsignal@1.0.0"

searchDocs.title: 2. Install​
searchDocs.content: wally install

searchDocs.title: 3. Add Packages to your project​
searchDocs.content: Make sure your default.project.json includes Wally packages:  { "name": "YourProject", "tree": { "$className": "DataModel", "ReplicatedStorage": { "Packages": { "$path": "Packages" } } } }

searchDocs.title: Using with roblox-ts​
searchDocs.content: Install the package:  npm install @rbxts/acidsignal   Then import in your code:  import Signal from "@rbxts/acidsignal"; const signal = Signal.new<[string]>(); signal.Connect((value) => { print("fired:", value); }); signal.Fire("hello");

searchDocs.title: Creating a Signal​
searchDocs.content: local Signal = require(path.to.AcidSignal) local signal = Signal.new()

searchDocs.title: Connecting a Callback​
searchDocs.content: local connection = signal:Connect(function(value) print("fired:", value) end)

searchDocs.title: Firing a Signal​
searchDocs.content: signal:Fire("hello") -- fired: hello

searchDocs.title: Disconnecting​
searchDocs.content: connection:Disconnect()

searchDocs.title: Once​
searchDocs.content: Use Once to connect a callback that automatically disconnects after the first fire:  signal:Once(function(value) print("fired once:", value) end) signal:Fire("hello") -- fired once: hello signal:Fire("hello") -- nothing

searchDocs.title: Wait​
searchDocs.content: Use Wait to yield the current thread until the signal fires:  local value = signal:Wait() print(value) -- "hello"   Pass a timeout in seconds to avoid yielding forever:  local value = signal:Wait(5) if not value then print("timed out!") end

searchDocs.title: Bound Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Pass extra arguments to Connect or Once to have them appended to every call:  signal:Connect(function(value, tag) print(value, tag) end, "mytag") signal:Fire("hello") -- hello mytag

searchDocs.title: DisconnectAll​
searchDocs.content: Disconnect all connections from a signal at once:  signal:DisconnectAll()

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: Alias for DisconnectAll:  signal:Destroy()
